governance.constitution:
- Refine's components are model (entities), process (supervisor to manage running processes), prompts (LLM templates), surfaces (interfaces into refine), tools (reusable functions for workflow steps), and workflow (defined workflow which calls out to tools). These map directly to src/[model| process|prompts|surfaces|tools|workflow].
- Refine uses a flat file persistence, file-based indexes, in-memory caching, and Rust to maintain high performance. Ensure <50ms performance on CLI and API calls (assuming we are not waiting on LLMs or outside tools).
- Ensure that the architecture is maintained and is consistent. Do not invent new architectural concepts; instead, follow the existing architecture.
- Ensure that documentation, especially src/intent/*, is maintained and the existing document format is preserved.
- Ensure Refine remains "agent-first" by using installed coding-agent CLIs. Do not duplicate coding agent functionality.
governance.product: Refine is a local-first, agent-first operating layer for software delivery. It moves user-defined Goals through a workflow to ensure parallel implementation across Nodes, quality, and governance.

findings.description: The plan hydrates the Controls options at initialization and centralizes successful activation, but it does not keep that registry projection current. Node settings create, rename, and archive currently refresh only the settings tab; the SSE project_updated payload/signature contains projection counts rather than Node registry or active identity; and api_mutation events have no browser listener. The new selector can therefore retain a removed name or omit a new Node in the same tab, while another browser on the same port can retain the wrong active label, Reporter context, and current-node data after activation.
findings.recommendation: Add one authoritative Node-context reconciliation path that rereads /api/nodes (and project status where needed), repopulates the selector, and is invoked after every local Node CRUD/activation plus attach/detach. Define a Node-specific SSE or a filtered api_mutation reconciliation for other clients, and test create/rename/archive plus two-client activation convergence.

findings.description: The proposed cache invalidation, Node-scoped reset, and current-surface reconciliation are underspecified for the actual SPA. refreshNodeScopedState currently clears chat, Reporter, dashboard, and current Goal state but redraws no route. Goals, Features, Logs, Changes, details, and settings have separate refresh paths; several reads lack a request generation fence, so an old-node GET can resolve after activation and overwrite the new-node render. A forced settings refresh can also overwrite a dirty Target App form, while New Goal, import, Feature, and detail modals can remain open across the ownership-context change.
findings.recommendation: Specify activation as one serialized transaction: persist the ID, reread authoritative identity, advance a Node-context generation or abort old reads, reset Node-owned state, then reconcile an explicit route/modal dispatch table. Preserve current/all/named URL semantics. Block or confirm switching when a Node-scoped draft is dirty, or explicitly preserve and safely rebind it. Add delayed-old-response and dirty/open-modal regressions.

findings.description: The verification list claims to retain the port-scoped active-Node contract but only schedules the static nav Rust test and mocked browser/VM behavior. It does not execute the existing backend regression that distinguishes the shared app-registry root from the port runtime root and proves activation, project status, current-node filtering, and new Goal ownership agree.
findings.recommendation: Add cargo test --lib surfaces::web_server::tests::project_runtime::project_status_uses_the_port_scoped_node_that_owns_and_filters_new_goals -- --exact to P3 and P4, and keep the selector browser test focused on the surface transition rather than treating a mocked POST as proof of runtime-root ownership.

result.summary: Keep P1's accessible Controls markup and focused Nav intent update, but revise P2-P4 before implementation. A Node switch is a runtime-shared context transition, not only a local select change: the plan must keep the Node registry and every browser client converged, fence old Node-scoped reads, define safe behavior for dirty forms and open modals, and execute the existing port-scoped ownership regression.

checklist.description: Add a cohesive src/surfaces/web/static/js/node-context.js module, loaded after common.js and before feature/router/init scripts, to own selector hydration and all Node-context transitions. Its forced reconciliation reads GET /api/project/status and GET /api/nodes with cache disabled, repopulates non-archived ID/display-name options, and runs after init, attach/detach, every local Node create/rename/archive/fleet update, and activation. Make settings_nodes.js delegate activation to the same serialized transaction: preflight local dirty surfaces, POST the selected node_id, advance a Node-context generation, invalidate cached projections, reread and validate authoritative identity, reset Reporter/chat/dashboard/current-detail state, update selector/brand/title, then refresh the current surface; an unchanged ID is a no-op, concurrent switches are disabled/coalesced, and failures restore the authoritative selection with an actionable error. Listen to the existing SSE api_mutation event, filter and debounce Node registry/activation plus attach/detach paths, and invoke the same reconciliation so other browser clients converge after create, rename, archive, or activation without adding a second durable authority.
checklist.governance_rationale: Guidance 0 requires the thin browser surface to delegate to the existing Node and project APIs and preserve runtime-local inspectable authority. Guidance 1 favors one focused Node-context module with a stable activation/reconciliation API over enlarging common.js or duplicating settings and Controls semantics.

affected_behavior: A delayed old-Node response cannot overwrite the new Node label, Reporter projection, table, detail, settings, or target-app state.
Dashboard and Goals retain their URL source of truth: current follows the new active Node while all and named filters remain unchanged.
Local switching never silently discards a dirty Node-scoped draft, and remote switching never allows a preserved stale draft to mutate under the new context.
Clean Goal, Feature, New Goal, import, and settings modal contexts close or refresh through an explicit route-aware transition instead of remaining bound to the old Node.
checklist.description: Fence Node-scoped asynchronous rendering with the coordinator generation and define one explicit post-switch route/modal dispatch table. Dashboard, Goals, Features, Logs, Changes, Reporter/target-app indicators, and settings loaders capture the generation before reads and silently discard late prior-generation results before mutating state or DOM. Reconcile Dashboard and Goals through their existing URL-backed current/all/named scope so switching changes the meaning of current only and never rewrites all or a named Node filter. For a local switch, reuse or expose focused guards for New Goal, recoverable import operations, Target App settings, Goal round edits, and Feature autosave: require confirmation before discarding dirty work and cancel activation if the user keeps editing; close clean Node-owned detail/create modals before route refresh. An external SSE-detected switch cannot be vetoed, so preserve any dirty values, mark that surface stale, disable its mutation controls, and require explicit discard/reopen before submission while the shell, selector, and safe underlay reconcile immediately. Clean modals close and the route dispatcher refreshes the visible surface. Add generation checks to Goal/Feature detail loads and all listed route refreshes so delayed old-Node GETs cannot repaint after the switch.
checklist.governance_rationale: Guidance 0 requires context changes to remain recoverable and semantically consistent across thin browser surfaces. Guidance 1 keeps generation ownership and dispatch coordination in node-context.js while each feature file exposes only its own small guard or refresh hook.

criticism_resolutions.resolution: P2 now defines one forced authoritative project-status and Node-registry reconciliation path for init, attach/detach, all local Node CRUD/activation, and filtered/debounced api_mutation SSE notices. It explicitly tests create, rename, archive, and two-client activation convergence.

P2-P3 now define a serialized activation transaction, cache invalidation and authoritative reread, a Node-context generation fence for every Node-scoped route/detail read, an explicit URL-preserving route/modal dispatcher, confirmation or cancellation for local dirty drafts, and a stale disabled preservation state for dirty surfaces when another client changes the Node. Delayed-response and dirty/open-modal regressions are required.

P3-P4 now run the exact existing project_runtime test that separates the shared app-registry root from the port runtime root and proves activation, project status, current-node filtering, and new Goal ownership agree; mocked browser POST coverage is limited to surface-transition behavior.

result.summary: Add an accessible Node selector immediately beside Reporter in the main Controls menu and back it with one cohesive browser Node-context coordinator. The coordinator will treat Node IDs as authoritative, reconcile project status plus the non-archived Node registry after local CRUD, activation, attach/detach, and filtered api_mutation SSE notices, serialize switches, fence old Node-scoped reads, protect dirty drafts and open modals, and dispatch an explicit URL-preserving refresh for every affected route. Focused VM/browser regressions and the existing port-runtime Rust test will prove both surface behavior and authoritative ownership.

checklist.evidence: Added the accessible, test-addressable global-node select immediately before Reporter; it renders non-archived Node display names backed by Node IDs, disables to No node when detached, updates only the Nav intent page, and extends the static navigation contract. The focused real-browser case was attempted and explicitly skipped because no Playwright Chromium build is available.

Added the 288-line cohesive node-context.js coordinator after common.js. It forces uncached project-status and Node-registry reconciliation on init, attachment changes, local Node CRUD/fleet changes, and filtered/debounced api_mutation notices; settings activation delegates to its serialized/coalesced ID transaction with exact POST payload, authoritative reread/validation, cache invalidation, rollback, and two-client convergence. Focused VM tests pass 11/11.

Added Node-context generation fences to Dashboard, Goals, Features, Logs, Changes, Reporter/project status, Goal and Feature detail reads, settings loads, Target App, and agent status. URL-backed current/all/named scopes are never rewritten. Local dirty Node-owned surfaces can veto before POST; confirmed local switches safely discard/cancel and close; external changes preserve dirty values, mark them stale, disable mutation controls, and leave the shell authoritative. Feature autosave is generation-fenced and delayed prior-generation results are discarded.

Ran both exact Rust contracts, the focused 11-case coordinator suite, the complete web regression suite, both requested browser patterns, Rust formatting, diff hygiene, status/stat, trailing-whitespace checks for new files, and final diff inspection. Scope is limited to the Controls selector, cohesive coordinator and feature hooks, tests, and the affected Nav intent page; Chromium absence is recorded as a skip.
